title: Skills in {name}: ready-made ones, your own, and when they’re used
description: A skill is how you want one kind of thing done, saved so that {name} does it the same way every time. The ready-made ones, adding yours, and where they’re kept.
answer: A skill is how you want one kind of thing done, saved so that {name} does it the same way every time: a weekly report, a letter in your style. {name} comes with ready-made ones, and you can add your own. When a request matches a skill, the brain follows its steps; type / in the box to name one yourself.
show.add: {settings} › {skills} › {add}: make one with {name}, take one from a file, or from a site.
parts: A text file named SKILL.md, in plain words: its name, when to follow it, then its steps, and sometimes other texts it needs beside it. It holds words only, never a program. It is an open format that other AI apps read too, so a skill written for one of them can come into {name}, and yours can go to them.

For every day, such as Formal letter, Budget and In plain words; for work, such as Project plan and What could go wrong; for learning, such as Flash cards and Study plan; and to draw and present, such as Chart, Slides, PowerPoint and Make a game. They work from your first request: when one fits, the brain reads it and it joins your skills; a message says so, with {see} to open its page. Visual answers is there from the start.
How do I add my own?

Ask {name} to save how something was done, in your own words. The third time you ask for the same kind of thing, {name} offers it too. Or open {settings} › {skills} › {add}: {make} asks you a few questions, then saves it with an example to try; {file} takes a SKILL.md that someone you trust sent you; {site} takes one that a site or an organisation publishes.

{site} reads what a few chosen sources publish for work: small business, marketing, sales, human resources, legal work and customer support. Press {browse} to see them; below them, type a site’s address, its skills index or a GitHub repository, and press {source} to see its skills too. None comes in until you have read its steps and pressed {adding}, and your requests are compared with them on this device.

With each request, the brain has the list of your skills, each with its name and when it is followed. When a request matches one, it reads that skill’s steps and follows them. To choose yourself, type / in the box and pick a skill by its name: it is followed for that message. A skill turned off is never followed.

In this browser, on this device, encrypted, with the rest of your work: each skill is a SKILL.md in a folder of its own. One you make or add in a project of yours stays in it; the others are in every project. They go into your backups, and {sync} takes them to your other computers. {save}, on a skill’s page, gives you its SKILL.md to keep or to pass on.
good: {skills} is one of the capabilities {name} offers when a moment calls for it. To have it sooner, turn it on in {settings} › {capabilities}: see {can}.

{settings} › {skills} says which skill was followed last, then lists them all. The page of one of yours shows {when}, an example with {try}, its steps and how many times it was followed: {edit} changes it there, and {change} opens a task to change it together.
A ready-made skill keeps up with {name}’s updates, and can’t be deleted, only turned off, with the switch at the top of its page. To change one, ask {name} in a task: from then on it is yours.
With a brain in the cloud, the list of your skills goes with each request, and a skill’s steps when it is followed: see {sees}.
At work, your organisation may add sources of its own, which you can’t remove, or keep to them alone.
fixes: A SKILL.md starts with its name, in small letters, digits and hyphens, and with when to follow it. Open the file in a text editor to check, or ask the person who sent it.
A skill from a site can’t be added
It runs programs, which can’t run here, or what was downloaded isn’t what its source lists. Only skills made of words can come in.
Check its address. GitHub lets a browser read it only so many times an hour: {name} tries again later by itself.
On its page, press {edit} and say under {when} what kind of request it is for, in a few clear words. Or name it with / in the box: then it is followed for that message.
ask: Which skills do I have, and when do you follow each one?
